_notice: HAND-MAINTAINED. This is the ONLY alias file anyone edits by hand for Hub-wide name checking. It is merged with the aliases already recorded in msh-compare-data/data/supplier-seed.json to produce company-alias-registry.json, which is GENERATED - never edit the registry.
_rules: Every entry needs canonical, variants, reason, evidence and addedOn. company_alias.py build EXITS 1 if any of those are missing - that is the evidence floor, not a formality.
evidence must be a URL you have actually opened, or the words 'seed:<supplier name>' when the fact is already recorded in supplier-seed.json.

Never add a variant on a hunch that two names look like the same company. Medtech is full of near-identical names (Pentax Medical UK Ltd is not Pentax UK Ltd). If you cannot evidence it, leave it unresolved - an unresolved name is a question, a wrong merge is a published error.

A pure legal-suffix or punctuation variant (Ltd / Limited / plc / & vs and / (UK)) does NOT need an entry here - the resolver strips those mechanically. Only add entries for things normalisation cannot reach: renames, acquisitions, trading names, brand-vs-entity, and genuinely different wordings.

If the company IS a Hub supplier, the better fix is to add the alias to its record in supplier-seed.json (see [[supplier-index-aliases-must-live-in-seed]]) so the compare tab gets it too. Use this overlay for companies not in the seed, or when the seed cannot be edited right now.

_ambiguous_rules: Two DIFFERENT real companies can genuinely share a name. Those are declared here so the resolver keeps returning AMBIGUOUS for them instead of quietly picking one - and so that a NEW, accidental collision still fails the build.
Declaring an ambiguity is not a way to silence the gate. It means: someone checked Companies House, found two real companies, and wrote down which is which. Same evidence floor as an alias entry.
An AMBIGUOUS name never publishes as-is. Use the distinguishing name (the full registered name, or name plus company number).
